LESSON: WRITING 14.4.1 GUIDED WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.4: Writing 14.4.1 Guided Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 14.4.1 Guided Writing, part of Strand 14 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to write meaningful sentences? 2. What makes it easy to write clear sentences?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 14.4.1 Guided Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and Imagination: The learner explores as they practise writing sentences from a substitution table.

Values:
Unity: cooperation is enhanced as the learner works collaboratively with others in writing sentences from a substitution table in groups.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life-skills: Self-esteem is nurtured as learners write correct sentences for effective communication.

Link to other learning areas:

Learner is able to relate the writing skill to writing effectively in all other learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources

Manual alphabet chart, flash cards, internet, posters, online dictionaries, assistive devices fitted with appropriate technologies such as hearing aids and

amplifiers, adapted course books, flash cards, sign language dictionary, internet, signed audio-visual recordings.
